title: Missions of Love
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Third-year junior high student Yukina Himuro, known as cold and aloof, secretly writes popular cell-phone novels and needs romance experience for her stories. She discovers that charming student-council president Shigure Kitami toys with girls who confess to him, and blackmails him into acting out romantic 'missions'. A love triangle forms with her cousin Akira, while Shigure's stepbrother Hisame and childhood friend Mami complicate things.
life_message: Real love grows from knowing a person honestly, not from scripts, schemes or control.

content.note: Emotional drama; Yukina's childhood trauma about her glasses (Wikipedia).
ANN reviewer (via Wikipedia) called it 'much racier' and an unequal romance; MangaUpdates lists Mature and Seduction. Junior high characters.
Mami's social anxiety and abandonment by her mother (Wikipedia).
Blackmail as the romance's engine (Wikipedia; AniList and MangaUpdates Blackmail); Shigure toys with girls' feelings.

dominant: Manipulation versus genuine love; teen romance; love triangle

frames.aligns: Yukina learns love is a gift, not a mission to extract.
frames.concerns: Racy scenes among junior high students; blackmail as romance.

frames.aligns: Pride (Yukina, Shigure) broken down over time.
Talking point on honesty in relationships.
Lying and manipulation shown to harm.
frames.concerns: Physical romance and seduction outside marriage.

frames.aligns: Right speech: false faces bring suffering.

frames.concerns: Coercion and consent; sexualization of minors.

frames.aligns: Honesty as the basis of relationships.

frames.concerns: Sexual content for a children's-award manga.

frames.aligns: Makoto: sincerity triumphs over false faces.

frames.concerns: Unwanted advances run against the Eleven Rules.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Reputation and secrets traded as leverage, but no violent honor code.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Teens make their own romantic rules outside adult oversight.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Cousin Akira's family bond vs school ties.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: School popularity ranks; Shigure pressured by family hospital inheritance (Wikipedia).

folkways.japan: Student council prestige, family succession to a hospital and keitai shōsetsu (cell-phone novels) reflect Japanese school and media culture of the 2000s.

delivery.evidence: Reviewers describe romance tropes and a 'heart in the right place', not lessons (Wikipedia reception) (to verify).

personified.ideology: Love as a game of conquest

delivery.note: Manipulative views of love are held by love interests who change rather than by flat villains.

winners_losers: Yukina and Shigure end together after honesty replaces the missions; Akira and Mami lose in love but grow.
